column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/python-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name>
# WHAT THIS PINS
#   Three jobs, one dependency each on `bump`: bump -> {ship, publish-withheld}.
#   `bump` is gated only on the actor (bot loop-break). `ship` and
#   `publish-withheld` share the SAME positive precondition
#   (`needs.bump.outputs.bumped == 'true'`) and carry opposite privacy guards,
#   so together they partition the bumped case: exactly one of them selects
#   whenever a bump happened, and neither selects when it did not.
# THE PRIVACY AXIS IS NOW LIVE — THIS FILE PREVIOUSLY RECORDED IT AS INERT.
#   Until 2026-08-17 `github.event.repository.private` appeared in this workflow
#   only inside `runs-on:` (runner routing, which gates nothing), so a private
#   repo bumped, tagged, pushed AND published its source to pypi.org. The old
#   header said so and said the fix, if it came, belonged in the workflow with
#   private-bump-publishes-anyway flipping to expect-skip=ship in the same PR.
#   That is this change: the row flipped, and it was renamed to
#   private-bump-withheld because "publishes anyway" is no longer true.
#   The risk is DISCLOSURE, not merely consistency: python-publish runs
#   `uv build` (which emits an sdist — a source tarball) then `uv publish`, and
#   PyPI has no unpublish. A release can be yanked, but its files stay
#   downloadable and the (name, version) pair is burned forever.
# WHY THERE IS A publish-withheld JOB AND WHY IT IS ASSERTED HERE
#   A bare `&& !private` would have converted every private caller to
#   silently-not-publishing — the exact defect this linter was written for
#   (graphql-synthesizer, 2026-08-08: green run, bumped, tagged, published
#   nothing, nothing said so). publish-withheld runs precisely when ship is
#   withheld, so the skip is a statement. Rows private-bump-withheld and
#   private-bump-opt-in are kept as a PAIR: one asserts the guard fires AND
#   announces itself, the other asserts the escape hatch actually escapes.
#   Neither row alone shows that, and "the guard is escapable" is the finding
#   that makes adding the guard safe.
# inputs.publish-from-private IS DECLARED IN EVERY ROW, including the rows where
# it cannot matter. An undeclared context path is an ERROR in this linter by
# design — silence about an axis is not a claim about it — and declaring it
# everywhere means a future condition that starts reading it in another cell
# already has the axis under assertion instead of quietly defaulting.
# always() IS DECLARED IN EVERY ROW because publish-withheld calls it. Note
# what this table can and cannot show about it: the linter has no failure model
# beyond the status functions a condition names, and this workflow names only
# always(), so the run these rows CANNOT express is the one always() actually
# exists for here — `bump` failing after setting `bumped=true` (bump step ok,
# commit/tag/push red), where needs-propagation would otherwise suppress the
# notice. What the rows below DO pin is the other half: that always() has not
# turned the notice into noise on every run where nothing was bumped.
# 1. The happy path. A public repo bumped, so it ships; nothing is withheld.
public-bump
# 2. THE FLIPPED ROW. Private, no opt-in: ship is withheld AND SAYS SO.
#    This is the row the old table predicted would flip when the guard landed.
private-bump-withheld
# 3. THE ESCAPE HATCH. Private, opt-in true: ship runs, and the withheld notice
#    stands down so a real publish is never accompanied by a claim it did not
#    happen. Without this row the guard would be indistinguishable from an
#    unconditional block on every private repo.
private-bump-opt-in
# 4. Nothing to release: bump ran and reported no version change. Neither
#    downstream job selects — publish-withheld must NOT announce a withholding
#    when there was nothing to publish in the first place.
public-no-bump
# 5. The private half of row 4. Privacy must stay inert in the no-bump cell:
#    a private repo with nothing to ship gets no notice either.
private-no-bump
# 6. Loop-break: the bot's own push must not re-trigger a release. `bump` is
#    skipped by actor; the empty `bumped` value models a SKIPPED upstream, which
#    is distinct from 'false'. `ship` skips by needs-propagation.
#    publish-withheld does NOT get to skip that way — its always() lifts it out
#    of needs-propagation — so it is its own `bumped == 'true'` clause that
#    stands it down. Asserting it here is what proves always() did not turn the
#    notice into noise on every bot push.
bot-actor-no-loop
# 7. The private bot push. Same as row 6 on the privacy axis flipped: with
#    always() in play, private + bot is the one cell where a naive complement
#    job WOULD fire (private is true, opt-in is false, bump is skipped), so this
#    row pins that the shared `bumped == 'true'` precondition holds it back.
bot-actor-private-no-loop
